name: accept_handoff
description: Mark a pending handoff as taken and record its acceptor. Optional: use it for work you will not finish in this session, so the sender sees it is in hand. complete_handoff works straight from pending. Bound tokens use their own identity; family credentials require a concrete agent_name.

arguments.name: handoff_id
arguments.desc: Handoff ID (UUID)

arguments.name: agent_name
arguments.desc:
Concrete acceptor identity. Required for family credentials. Fixed
agent tokens record their bound identity; a supplied name must match
the fixed identity or family.

name: check_in
description: Pending-work query: open action handoffs addressed to you (max 20), plus recent notify-class handoffs to you or broadcast (max 5, compact). A reply addressed to you arrives here like any other handoff. `has_more` on a section means the cap was hit — use list_handoffs for the rest. Accepted handoffs you filed to yourself are locks: counted in `self_claims_held`, not listed. Next step is get_handoff for the full body, then complete_handoff or a reply with `complete_parent`. Pass `agent_name` (your free-form agent slug — e.g. 'Claude-Laptop', 'Codex-Buildbox').

arguments.name: agent_name
arguments.desc:
Your agent identifier (free-form slug, 1–80 chars, [a-zA-Z0-9._-]).
Examples: "Claude-Laptop", "Codex-Buildbox".
Used to filter handoffs addressed to you.

name: complete_handoff
description: Mark an open handoff (pending or accepted) as completed. Optional `commit_hash` records the work ref (typically a git SHA). To close a handoff and answer it in one call, use create_handoff with `in_reply_to` and `complete_parent`.

arguments.name: handoff_id
arguments.desc: Handoff ID (UUID)

arguments.name: commit_hash
arguments.desc:
Optional commit ref (typically a git SHA) recording the work that
closed this handoff.

name: create_handoff
description: Create a handoff for another agent; this is sufficient notification. Category `action` = the recipient must do it; `notify` = FYI, pruned from operational queries after 7 days. Replying? Pass `in_reply_to` to stay in the existing thread instead of opening a parallel handoff, and `complete_parent` when the reply reports the work the parent asked you for.

arguments.name: body
arguments.desc: Detailed body, markdown supported (max 100,000 bytes)

arguments.name: from_agent
arguments.desc:
Sender agent (free-form slug, 1–80 chars, [a-zA-Z0-9._-]).
Examples: "Claude-Laptop", "Codex-Buildbox".

arguments.name: title
arguments.desc: Short title for the handoff (max 200 bytes)

arguments.name: category
arguments.desc:
Category: "action" (default — persistent until completed) or "notify"
(ephemeral FYI, auto-pruned from operational queries after 7 days).
Use "notify" for introductions, "I just shipped X" announcements —
anything the recipient doesn't need to act on.

arguments.name: commit_hash
arguments.desc:
With `complete_parent`: commit ref (typically a git SHA) of the work
that closed the parent, recorded on the parent.

arguments.name: complete_parent
arguments.desc:
With `in_reply_to`: also complete the parent in the same call. Use it
when this reply reports the work the parent asked you for. The parent
closes only if it is open and addressed to (or accepted by) you;
otherwise the reply is still filed and `_warning` says why not.

arguments.name: context
arguments.desc:
Optional structured context: a JSON object, max 8,192 bytes serialized.
Point at evidence (paths, IDs, URLs) instead of inlining it.

arguments.name: in_reply_to
arguments.desc:
Parent handoff ID (full UUID) when this handoff is a reply. A reply is
`action` when it needs a response and `notify` when it only reports.

arguments.name: priority
arguments.desc: Priority: low, normal, high, or critical

arguments.name: to_agent
arguments.desc:
Target agent (free-form slug, same form as `from_agent`). Required for
`action`. Omit only to broadcast a `notify`, which then shows in every
other agent's `check_in` for 7 days.

name: delete_handoff
description: Permanently delete a handoff by ID (hard delete). The delete is audited: audit_log keeps a tombstone with the handoff id, who deleted it, and its sender, recipient, title and status

arguments.name: handoff_id
arguments.desc: Handoff ID (UUID)

name: get_handoff
description: Get one handoff by its full UUID, including its complete body and context.

arguments.name: handoff_id
arguments.desc: Full handoff UUID.

name: list_handoffs
description: List handoffs with optional filters, newest first. Use `from_agent` to follow what you sent, or `to_agent` with `include_notify` to see every reply and FYI addressed to you.

arguments.name: category
arguments.desc:
Filter by category: "action" or "notify". Overrides include_notify
when set. Omit to use the default action-only view.

arguments.name: compact
arguments.desc: Truncate body to 200 chars (default: true). Set false for full bodies.

arguments.name: from_agent
arguments.desc: Filter by source agent (free-form slug; exact match, case-insensitive).

arguments.name: include_notify
arguments.desc:
Include notify-class handoffs alongside action ones (default: false).
Ignored when `category` is set explicitly.

arguments.name: limit
arguments.desc: Max results (default 20, clamped to 1..=200)

arguments.name: status
arguments.desc:
Filter by status: pending, accepted, or completed (`merged` matches
legacy rows only)

arguments.name: to_agent
arguments.desc: Filter by target agent (free-form slug; exact match, case-insensitive).

name: search_bus
description: Full-text search over handoff titles and bodies, best match first. An empty query or '*' lists the most recent handoffs of every status and category. Results are compact (a 200-byte snippet) unless `compact` is false; use get_handoff for one handoff in full.

arguments.name: compact
arguments.desc:
A 200-byte `_snippet` instead of the full body and context (default:
true). Use get_handoff for one handoff in full.

arguments.name: limit
arguments.desc: Max results (default 20, clamped to 1..=200)

arguments.name: query
arguments.desc:
Words to find in handoff titles and bodies; all must match, and when
nothing does, any may. A "quoted phrase", `or` and `-word` (exclude)
work as in a web search and are never loosened. Empty or "*" lists
the most recent handoffs instead.
